hook: Limestone bluffs up to 120 feet tall created a major barrier to Kansas City's urban expansion.

sections.voiceover: Limestone bluffs up to 120 feet tall created a major barrier to Kansas City's urban expansion.
b_roll: Historical map showing the Missouri River and towering bluff barriers

sections.voiceover: Along the Missouri River, rock walls trapped urban expansion. Kansas City Mayor Milton Payne allocated nearly an entire year's budget to cut the bluffs. Who could break through 120 feet of stone?
b_roll: Archival illustration of Missouri River bluffs blocking 1850s city development
Historical portrait of Mayor Milton Payne beside civic ledger entries from 1855
Diagram highlighting 120 feet vertical height of the rock wall

sections.voiceover: However, Father Bernard Donnelly recruited hundreds of Irish immigrants so they'd dig through the bluffs.
b_roll: Archival sketch of Father Bernard Donnelly standing with quarry workers

sections.voiceover: Payne paved a quarter mile of levee using 1855 funds.
b_roll: Historical drawing of Irish laborers digging through limestone cliffs
Animated map showing newly carved street corridors reaching the waterfront
Graphic marker highlighting a paved quarter-mile levee along the river bank

sections.voiceover: Donnelly's Irish laborers carved streets through the 120-foot limestone bluffs to expand Kansas City.
b_roll: Wide shot of modern Kansas City streets cutting through historical bluffs
